name: Form-Fill from Intake Data

parameters.content:
## Form-Fill from Intake Data

### How it works

1. The workflow triggers when an intake form is submitted via webhook.
2. It validates and normalizes the submitted intake data.
3. Depending on validation and configuration, it builds a list of documents to auto-fill and processes each document accordingly.
4. Documents are either filled and copied in Google Drive or prepared for signatures through DocuSign.
5. The resulting documents are aggregated, logged for compliance, and an attorney notification email is sent.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure the webhook trigger to receive intake form submissions.
- [ ] Set up and configure credentials for Google Drive API for document manipulation.
- [ ] Set up and configure credentials for DocuSign API for envelope creation and signing.
- [ ] Configure the compliance audit sub-workflow to log document fills as needed.
- [ ] Add email credentials to enable notification sending to attorneys.

### Customization

Edit the 'Build Document Fill List' node to customize which documents to generate for each practice area based on your needs.

## Receive and validate intake

Starts the workflow by capturing intake form data via webhook, confirms it has the minimum fields needed (full_name, email, matter_type), then looks up templates. If required fields are missing, skips document generation entirely rather than creating partial or blank documents.

## Build the document fill list

Maps this intake's practice area to the firm's configured document templates. If no templates are configured for this practice area, skips document generation rather than erroring.

## Split and route each document

Fans out into one item per configured document, then routes each one by method: DocuSign for the retainer, Google Docs for everything else.

## DocuSign path — draft the retainer

Creates the retainer as a draft envelope with fields pre-filled from the template — status 'created', never 'sent'. The attorney reviews and sends it manually from inside DocuSign.

## Google Docs path — fill and export

For every non-retainer document: copies the template, replaces every {{merge_tag}} with the intake's data, and exports the filled copy as a PDF for review.

## Combine, log, and deliver

Waits for both the Google Docs path and the DocuSign path to finish, combines every generated PDF plus the DocuSign draft reference into one email, logs the run to the OPS1 audit sheet, then delivers to the attorney for review.

nodes.name: When Intake Form Is Submitted
nodes.notes:
Receives the intake submission that triggers document form-filling.

Uses the same field names as the Clio Intake Sync template — if you've already deployed that one, point this webhook at the same Fluent Forms feed (or add a second webhook action for the same form) and both templates read identical data.

Fluent Forms setup: Settings → Integrations → Webhook → Add New → paste this node's Production URL → Method POST → Format JSON.

Expected fields: full_name, email, matter_type (required); phone, case_details, referral_source (optional).

nodes.name: Validate And Normalize Intake Data
nodes.notes:
Confirms the intake has the minimum fields needed to fill any document at all: full_name, email, matter_type.

practice_area is read directly from matter_type — keep your form's matter-type field values matching the keys you use in TEMPLATE_MAP below (case-sensitive is not required, but exact spelling is).

Output: is_valid_intake is false (and the run is skipped) if any required field is missing.

nodes.name: If Intake Data Is Valid
nodes.notes:
Yes (full_name, email, and matter_type all present) → look up which templates apply.
No (a required field is missing) → route to Skip. Better to skip than generate a document with a blank client name.

nodes.name: Skip Invalid Intake Payload
nodes.notes: The intake submission was missing full_name, email, or matter_type — most likely a form field-mapping issue. No documents generated. Check the intake form's field names against the deploy guide if this keeps happening.

nodes.name: Build Document Fill List
nodes.notes:
Looks up TEMPLATE_MAP by this intake's practice_area to decide which documents to generate.

If a practice area isn't in the map at all, or its templates' n8n Variables aren't set yet, docs comes back empty and nothing is generated -- this is a safe default, not an error.

Edit the TEMPLATE_MAP object directly in this node's code to add practice areas or documents as your firm's template library grows.

nodes.name: If Templates Are Configured
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one template is configured for this practice area) → generate the documents.
No (practice area not in TEMPLATE_MAP, or its template Variables aren't set) → route to Skip. Nothing to fill.

nodes.name: Skip No Templates Configured
nodes.notes: This practice area has no documents configured in TEMPLATE_MAP, or the relevant TEMPLATE_*_DOC_ID Variables aren't set yet. No documents generated. Add a row to TEMPLATE_MAP (or set the missing Variable) if this practice area should have documents.

nodes.name: Split Into Single Document Items
nodes.notes: Turns the single 'docs' array into separate items -- one per document to fill -- so each one runs through its own fill chain independently. Every item still carries the full intake data (full_name, email, etc.) plus its own doc_label, method, and template_doc_id.

nodes.name: If Document Uses DocuSign
nodes.notes: Routes the retainer (method: 'docusign') to the DocuSign draft-envelope path, and every other configured document (method: 'google_docs') to the existing copy/merge/export path. Both paths converge at 'Aggregate Filled Documents'.

nodes.name: Fetch DocuSign Account Info
nodes.notes:
Every DocuSign API call needs the account's base_uri and account_id, which vary per account and aren't fixed URLs -- this looks them up fresh each run rather than hardcoding them.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'OAuth2 API' → Grant Type: Authorization Code → Authorization URL: '{DOCUSIGN_AUTH_BASE_URL}/oauth/auth' → Access Token URL: '{DOCUSIGN_AUTH_BASE_URL}/oauth/token' → Client ID/Secret from a DocuSign Integration Key (DocuSign Admin → Apps and Keys → Add App/Integration Key) → Scope: 'signature' → Connect my account. Save as 'DocuSign account'.

DOCUSIGN_AUTH_BASE_URL is 'https://account-d.docusign.com' for a developer/demo sandbox account, or 'https://account.docusign.com' for production -- most firms should start with the sandbox for testing.

Response includes accounts[0].base_uri and accounts[0].account_id, read explicitly by the next step.

nodes.name: Build DocuSign Envelope Request
nodes.notes:
Constructs the envelope request body. If your retainer template's field labels differ from full_name/email/phone/practice_area/case_details/date, edit the tabLabel values in textTabs to match -- DocuSign matches by exact label text, not by field order.

DOCUSIGN_RETAINER_ROLE_NAME (n8n Variable) must match the signer role name defined on your DocuSign template exactly (e.g. 'Client', 'Signer 1') -- check your template in DocuSign if unsure.

Set to 'Run Once for Each Item' -- if your firm ever configures more than one DocuSign document type, this makes sure every one of them gets processed, not just the first.

nodes.name: Post DocuSign Draft Envelope
nodes.notes:
Creates the retainer as a draft envelope in DocuSign -- status 'created', not 'sent'. Nothing is emailed to the client and nothing is signed by this call; the attorney opens DocuSign, reviews the pre-filled draft under Manage → Drafts, edits if needed, and sends it manually.

Uses the same 'DocuSign account' credential as the account-info lookup.

Response: { envelopeId, uri, statusDateTime, status } -- read explicitly by the next step.

nodes.name: Prepare DocuSign Result Data
nodes.notes: Carries the envelope ID forward so the review email can tell the attorney exactly which draft to look for in DocuSign. Set to 'Run Once for Each Item' -- see 'Build DocuSign Envelope Request' notes.

nodes.name: Copy Google Docs Template
nodes.notes:
Duplicates the Google Doc template so the merge step below can safely replace text without ever touching your original template. 'Copy In The Same Folder' is off, with Parent Drive set to My Drive and Parent Folder set to GENERATED_DOCS_FOLDER_ID (an n8n Variable) — create one folder for this once and reuse it for every intake. The rename (File Name field) and destination folder are both top-level fields on this node, not under Options — an earlier version of this template nested them under Options, which n8n silently ignored (files landed with the default "Copy of ..." name, loose in Drive root).

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'Google Drive' → select 'Google Drive OAuth2 API'. Same setup pattern as the Google Sheets credential used by the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) — create an OAuth client in Google Cloud Console, enable the Google Drive API AND the Google Docs API (both, since 'Merge Fields Into Copy' below needs Docs API access on this same credential), then connect. Save as 'Google Drive account'.

Response: { id, name, mimeType } — id is the new copy's document ID, read explicitly by the next two steps (this node's own output replaces the intake data, so downstream steps reference the intake fields via 'Split Into One Item Per Document' by name, not $json). The filled copy is intentionally kept (not deleted) so the review email below can link directly to it for editing.

nodes.name: Build Merge Field Updates
nodes.notes:
Builds the list of find-and-replace operations sent to the Docs API in the next step.

Your Google Doc templates must contain these exact tags, typed literally into the document text: {{full_name}}, {{email}}, {{phone}}, {{practice_area}}, {{case_details}}, {{referral_source}}, {{date}}.

Add or remove entries in MERGE_FIELDS to match what your templates actually use -- an unused tag in this list is harmless (nothing to replace), but a tag in your template that's missing from this list will be left as literal {{text}} in the filled document.

Set to 'Run Once for Each Item' -- with more than one Google Docs template type configured, this makes sure every one of them gets merged, not just the first.

nodes.name: Update Google Doc Merge Fields
nodes.notes:
Replaces every merge tag in the copied document with the actual intake data.

n8n's native Google Docs node doesn't expose a find-and-replace / merge-fields operation (confirmed against n8n's own community forum — this is a known gap, not something we missed), so this one step still needs a direct API call. It reuses the exact same 'Google Drive account' credential as the Copy and Export steps on either side of it — no separate credential to set up, as long as the Google Docs API is enabled alongside Drive API in your Cloud Console project (see the Copy Template Document node's notes). Uses 'Predefined Credential Type' (not 'Generic Credential Type') since Google's OAuth2 credential isn't a generic-auth-compatible type — Generic silently sends no Authorization header at all.

This node's own response ({documentId, replies}) is a different shape than what the export step needs -- the export step reads new_doc_id explicitly from 'Build Merge Field Replacements', not from this node's output.

nodes.name: Export Document As PDF
nodes.notes:
Exports the filled document as a PDF using Drive's native export-on-download conversion (only works on native Google Docs/Sheets/Slides files, which the copy always is).

Uses the same 'Google Drive account' credential as the Copy and Merge steps — one credential covers the whole workflow.

Verify the 'Convert Google Docs to' option under this node's Options is set to PDF when you first open it in the n8n UI — the exact nested field layout for this option could not be confirmed against a live n8n instance during template authoring. Output lands in the binary property named 'data' by default, which 'Build Google Docs Result' below expects; if you rename it here, update that node's code to match.

nodes.name: Prepare Google Docs Result Data
nodes.notes: Converges here from the Google Docs path before joining the DocuSign path at Combine Document Results. Set to 'Run Once for Each Item' -- see 'Build Merge Field Replacements' notes.

nodes.name: Merge All Document Results
nodes.notes:
Waits for both the Google Docs path and the DocuSign path to finish, then combines every item from both into one list for Aggregate Filled Documents.

This explicit Merge node matters: two branches connected straight into the same input on a downstream node can run that node as soon as the FASTER branch finishes, before the slower one arrives -- silently dropping whichever document type takes longer (this happened during testing: the DocuSign draft was dropped from the review email because its branch finished after Aggregate had already run). A Merge node always waits for all of its inputs first.

nodes.name: Aggregate All Filled Documents
nodes.notes:
Runs once for all documents generated in this run (mode: Run Once for All Items) — receives the combined list from Combine Document Results, which waits for both the Google Docs path and the DocuSign path before this runs.

Assumes each Google Docs item's binary property is named 'data', matching the 'Put Output in Field' setting on Export Filled Document As PDF. If any one document's export failed, it's silently excluded rather than blocking the others — check execution history to see which one, if doc_count is lower than expected.

nodes.name: Log Document Fill To Audit
nodes.notes:
Calls the Bar-Compliance Guardrail to log this document-generation run to your compliance audit sheet.

This workflow delivers documents to your own attorney/reviewer, not a client -- so opt-out checking does not apply and approved will always be true here. The purpose of this call is the audit trail: which documents were generated, for whom, and when.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable (Settings → Variables).

nodes.name: Notify Attorney Of Documents
nodes.notes:
Delivers every filled document as a PDF attachment to the reviewing attorney.

toEmail reads FIRM_REVIEWER_EMAIL (falls back to FIRM_EMAIL if unset) -- never the intake submitter's own address, so the review copy always lands with your firm, not bounces back to the client.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → enter your email provider's settings → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

attachmentsBinary's 'property' field must name the binary property(s) to attach explicitly -- an empty entry attaches nothing, it does NOT mean 'attach everything' (confirmed live: this shipped broken until fixed). The expression above reads whatever file0, file1, ... keys Aggregate Filled Documents actually built, comma-separated, so it always attaches every generated PDF regardless of how many documents were configured.

body.case_details: Rear-ended on I-80 on 2026-07-15, ongoing physical therapy for whiplash.

description: Auto-populates the firm's own retainer, intake, and court cover sheet templates from intake form data — copies each configured Google Doc template, replaces {{merge_tag}} placeholders with the intake fields, exports as PDF, and emails every generated document to the attorney for review. Field population only — never drafts legal language, nothing sent to a client automatically. Replaces Lawyaw or Clio Draft ($70-119/mo). Logs every run to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet.
